links.outcome: Delirium prediction AUROC with vs without injected clinical knowledge report, and with random control reports
links.effect: Clinically meaningful knowledge report improved AUROC by 8.57 points (8B) and 1.99 points (70B); random control reports did not improve and often degraded performance.
links.quote: Adding a clinically meaningful external knowledge report improves AUROC by 8.57 percentage points for the 8B model and 1.99 percentage points for the 70B model compared to no external knowledge.

unlisted_practices: Using locally deployable open-weight LLMs with inference-time knowledge injection as a privacy-preserving alternative to frontier closed models
Using SHAP-based attribution to confirm injected knowledge is used in prediction

screen.reason: The study tests an inference-time deployment practice (injecting an external clinical knowledge report into prompts of existing models without retraining) compared to baseline prompting across MIMIC-IV ICU admissions for delirium prediction.
